claim: An enrolled device-bound relay admin can inspect and change one managed room from a remote Syzygy installation through a separately action-signed, exact-revision, one-message control channel. Five real Yjs clients converge across rapid edits and a two-client partition/rejoin while viewer writes remain blocked and awareness recovers without server persistence.

proved: The remote control route is separate from the Yjs room route, accepts at most 64 KiB, one strict text request, and one bounded JSON response.
The ordinary v4 connection proof is consumed before the server permits administration; only an active device-bound admin authorization is accepted.
A second Ed25519 signature binds the semantic action SHA-256, room, administrator member, exact revision, issue time, and the same one-use nonce under syzygy-relay-admin-action-v1.
Status, issue, rotate, and revoke have exact action shapes; stale revisions return a typed rejection and add no mutation.
Successful mutations durably replace and reload the registry, return a new capability only for issue/rotate, and evict every room peer for fresh reauthentication.
A viewer-role WebSocket transport drops outbound document-update frames while the relay independently rejects non-empty viewer writes; viewer reconnect still receives retained state.
The relay broadcasts y-websocket query-awareness on join so peers republish ephemeral presence without awareness storage.
Five device-bound clients converge after 60 rapid writes and connected/offline partition edits; awareness removal and bounded periodic recovery are observed.
The soak refreshes y-websocket's documented mutable connection parameters synchronously on close, so every automatic physical retry carries a new one-use proof instead of weakening replay denial.
The registry contains only SHA-256 capability digests after remote issue and rotation.
notProved: That an enrolled installation key belongs to a verified person or organization.
That the shared project-device directory approves or grants the relay admin role.
Administrator-key backup, escrow, recovery, or device-key rotation.
Trusted time, public TLS/WSS operations, automatic replacement-invitation delivery, hostile-frame fuzzing, backup administration, or third-party relay behavior.
Physical packaged two-install interaction; the five clients are distinct protocol/provider instances in one bounded harness process.
